title: set_parent_send result
description: What set_parent_send returns: the tracks whose parent send was switched, and what each of them now feeds. The target is reported per track rather than once, because the flag's destination is context-dependent — the enclosing folder parent for a track inside a folder, the master for one that is not — so the same call can mean two different things across its own selector list. A mutating tool, so it carries the undo report fields defined by messages/tool-result-undo.schema.json.

tracks.description: The tracks that were changed, in the order the call supplied them. All of them resolved: an unresolved or ambiguous selector refuses the whole call rather than applying it to part of the list.

enabled.description: The state that was applied, echoed because the consequence is asymmetric and the agent has to describe the right one: switching it off removes the track from the summed path without muting it, since explicit sends still carry signal.

silencedFolderParents.description: Folder parents left with no children feeding them as a result of this call. This is the shape that looks like a summing bus and sums nothing, and it is the condition that makes a render of that folder near-silent — so it is named here rather than discovered at render time. Empty in the ordinary case.

parentSendChange.description: One track's parent send change, naming what the flag routes to for that track.

name.description: Track name as shown in REAPER.

previousEnabled.description: The flag's state before the call. Equal to the applied state when the track was already in that state, which is a no-op worth not describing as a change.

target.description: What this track's parent send feeds: its enclosing folder parent, or the master track when it sits at top level.

trackReference.description: A track the tool acted on, named as well as identified. The GUID is what the agent addresses the track by on any follow-up call; the name is what it says to the producer, who cannot see a GUID. Returned even when the call supplied a GUID, because a name pattern resolves here rather than in the agent — a safe operation on a confident-but-imperfect match proceeds and this is how it reports which track it chose (Requirement 7.6).

name.description: Track name as shown in REAPER at the time of the call.

guid.description: A stable REAPER GUID, in REAPER's own braced form.

undoPositionBefore.description: REAPER undo stack position captured by the extension immediately before this tool applied its change. A "revert all AI changes" operation calls Undo_DoUndo2 in a loop until the stack is back at this position.

undoDescription.description: Undo point description the extension passed to Undo_EndBlock2 for this tool, persisted with the tool_result message so the chat UI can list what the agent changed.
